title: Cursor-based pagination for a note store
difficulty_rationale: New method plus a new exception in an existing class; requires stable keyset ordering, opaque cursor encoding/decoding and robustness to concurrent deletions.
summary: Add NoteStore.list_page(limit, cursor) using keyset (cursor) pagination ordered by (created_at, id).
required_behavior: Notes are ordered by (created_at, id) ascending.
list_page(limit, cursor=None) returns (notes, next_cursor); next_cursor is None when there are no further notes.
The cursor is an opaque URL-safe string; clients never parse it.
Paging with cursors visits every note exactly once even if notes that were already returned are deleted between calls, or new notes with later timestamps are added.
limit must be an int in 1..100, otherwise ValueError.
A malformed or tampered cursor raises InvalidCursor (a ValueError subclass exported from notes.store).

acceptance_tests.description: Walking all pages yields every note once in order.
The last page returns next_cursor None.
Equal timestamps are ordered by id.
Deleting a returned note does not skip unseen notes.
